clue.text: With ease supply water

definitions.note: a body of water, here an inlet of the Arctic Ocean off northern Russia

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters before it are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone is told to provide water effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal acting on WITH EASE. The White Sea is an arm of the Barents Sea in north-west Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a sea, and a sea is an expanse of water, so the clue defines it by its general class.

clue.text: A bowler — perhaps he had to accept a means of changing speed

definitions.note: a noun phrase naming one example of the answer, signalled by perhaps

indicators.note: to accept means the contracted form of the pronoun and verb takes the following letter into its middle

parts.note: he had contracts to he'd
a gear is the mechanism a driver uses to change speed

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler had to put up with some device for varying his pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricket bowler varying pace, but the bowler is the hat; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a round felt hat, and hats are one kind of covering worn on the head.

clue.text: Humiliate and demolish a girl

parts.note: to take down a building is to demolish it
Peg is a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to shame and wreck a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deflate someone's pride, which is to humble or humiliate them.

clue.text: One is remarkable

definitions.meaning: in grammar the number that refers to just one person or thing
unusual or extraordinary, a sense found in phrases like a ... achievement

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a word in the number for a lone item is so called, and the word also means extraordinary or exceptional.

clue.text: Split — see below

definitions.meaning: broken apart, as in torn in two pieces
a cross-reference in a document directing the reader to text further down

explanation.definitionFit: The word means into separate pieces, and read as two words it is the old cross-reference phrase meaning look further down the page.

clue.text: Slough, where other ranks enlisted in the service

indicators.note: enlisted in means the soldiers' abbreviation joins up inside the church word, as recruits join a unit

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: In the town of Slough, ordinary soldiers have joined up for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town west of London, but here it is a bog; 'the service' is a church service, not the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or boggy hollow, and a morass is likewise a marsh or quagmire.

clue.text: Heard story's end

indicators.note: heard means the word for a story is listened to rather than read, giving its same-sounding twin

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone has listened to how a story finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear part of something, as of an animal or a procession, is its end.

clue.text: Winkle's home to dispose of since he's been given accommodation

definitions.note: a winkle is a small sea snail, which lives in a shell

indicators.note: been given accommodation means the pair of short words are housed inside the trading verb

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it
as can mean since, as in as it was late
the pronoun he, with the 's read as has

explanation.surface: A man has to get rid of something now that he has been found lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Winkle sounds like a person's name, but a winkle is a small edible sea snail found on British shores.
explanation.definitionFit: A winkle is a marine snail and its protective casing found on the beach is where it lives.

clue.text: In olden days, anybody went in a coach

indicators.note: went in means the pronoun is placed inside the word for a coach, like a passenger boarding

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach, a horse-drawn coach
one means anybody, as in one can never tell

explanation.surface: Long ago, any traveller rode in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when tools were made from rock stands for the very distant past.

clue.text: The man to raise a flag

definitions.meaning: a common man, as in every man ...
to lift, as in to ... up a car
a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a fellow or workman, the verb for lifting a car on a lever, and a ship's small bow flag.

clue.text: Dubious characters selling amber and priceless stones

definitions.note: a collection of priceless marble sculptures

indicators.note: dubious characters means the letters of the words that follow are of doubtful order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Shady people are trading in amber and precious gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like shady people but is the letters themselves; 'Dubious' tells you to rearrange SELLING AMBER. The Elgin Marbles are classical Greek sculptures from the Parthenon held in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The sculptures taken from the Parthenon are carved in marble, so they are literally invaluable carved rock.

clue.text: Landlord invested in large buildings in more than one capital

indicators.note: invested in means the property owner is placed inside the word for big buildings

parts.note: blocks are large buildings, as in office blocks
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A property owner has put money into large buildings in several cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters written separately without joins are a style of upper-case writing used on forms.

clue.text: Draw back wind again?

definitions.meaning: to coil once more, as rope or wire, read as re plus coil

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to flinch or retreat in fear, and split up as re-coil it means to loop a rope a second time.

clue.text: Being cold in the past, settle comfortably

parts.note: ens is the philosophical term for being or existence
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
once means formerly, in the past

explanation.surface: Having been chilly earlier, someone now gets cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: ENS is the Latin-derived philosophical word for being or an entity, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To install oneself snugly in a place is to nestle securely, which is what settling comfortably means.

clue.text: King gathers a lot of soldiers, leaving 1.000 in store

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: leaving means the Roman numeral is left out of the phrase for many soldiers

parts.note: an army is a lot of soldiers
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A monarch assembles a large body of troops, with a thousand left behind in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops the thousand from the army phrase; 'gathers' only joins, and GR (Georgius Rex) is the usual crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for grain, so the clue defines it by its function as a place of storage.

clue.text: Newspaper produced during a disturbance involving article

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters wrap round the grammatical article
a disturbance stirs up the letters of the two words before it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A paper was printed in the middle of a riot that involved some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges DURING A, and 'involving' puts A, the indefinite article, inside that. The Guardian is a British national daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a UK national daily, so the clue defines it by the class of publication.

clue.text: Relieved after Henry left some petrol

indicators.note: left means the letter for the unit is departed from the word for relieved

parts.note: thankful means relieved, as in thankful it was over
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of electrical inductance

explanation.surface: Someone is glad once Henry has driven off with a bit of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a man's name but is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A container's capacity of fuel is a quantity of petrol, which is some petrol in amount.

clue.text: Oil producers, inter alia, show a capital deficiency

indicators.note: inter means bury, so the oil cartel is buried inside the Latin word

parts.note: taken as written
OPEC is the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

explanation.surface: Oil-producing nations, among other things, demonstrate a lack of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' reads as Latin for among other things, but 'inter' means bury; 'capital' is the head, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair loss from the scalp is a lack on the head, and capital comes from the Latin for head.

clue.text: Still shut up one end — that's odd!

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of the three words before it are set in a strange order

explanation.surface: Something remains sealed at one end, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges UP ONE END; 'that's' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never yet uncovered or unsealed is still closed, which is what still shut means.

clue.text: Many fly — that's correct

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
to fly is to hurry, to hasten

explanation.surface: Lots of insects are about, and that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect but is the verb meaning to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone in the sense of rebuking or disciplining them is to humble them by reproof.

clue.text: A stopper can be brought to move a little, if need be

parts.note: a tap is a plug or bung that stops a cask
to inch is to move a little at a time

explanation.surface: A bung can be made to shift slightly when necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an emergency or when necessary, which is the sense of if need be.

clue.text: Ambassador's sister at Number Ten

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, linking the definition

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, is a number
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, ten

explanation.surface: An envoy's nun sister is at the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence, but here 'Number' is C and 'Ten' is IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy accredited to a foreign government is the Pope's diplomatic representative, his ambassador.

clue.text: King giving honour to a chap

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A monarch awards a British decoration to some fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon is the king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare and folklore the ruler of the fairies is a monarch, so he is defined as a king.

clue.text: See and forget disastrous play 'For time"

indicators.note: disastrous means the three words before it are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A reviewer urges us to watch and then forget a terrible play called For Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a theatre piece but is part of the definition, to play for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay deliberately, dawdling to gain time, is the idiom's sense, matching stalling.

clue.text: White has a go

parts.note: a shy is an attempt or try, a go, as in a coconut shy

explanation.surface: The white player makes a move in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins: a white person or piece 'has a go' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is pale grey, so something ashen in colour is pale or white.

clue.text: "It's a feller!" "No way! It's a bird!"

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for a road is taken away from the man's name

parts.note: Ernest is a fellow's name
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Two people argue over whether something is a man or a bird, like spotting Superman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the old 'It's a bird! It's a plane!' gag.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a large bird of prey, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: A diamond he has — I have paste

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in cards
the 's of he's stands for has
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone owns a diamond, but the speaker has only a fake gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paste' looks like imitation jewellery, contrasting with the diamond, but it is glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a sticky substance for fixing things together, so it is a kind of glue.

clue.text: is artist in paradise turning left?

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembly is read backwards
in means the two short words sit inside the word for paradise

parts.note: Eden is the paradise of Genesis
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an artist in heaven is about to turn to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole assembly, EDISRAEN. In Britain, where traffic drives on the left, the nearside is the left side of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK usage the kerb side of a car is the left-hand side, hence the question mark.
